AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: We conducted a study at two main centres for paediatric surgery in the Republic of Ireland, Temple Street Children's University Hospital (TSCUH) and Our Lady's Children's Hospital Crumlin (OLCHC).

AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: The aim of the study was to assess doctors' opinions, frequency and methods of smartphone use in clinical practice.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Doctors (n = 265) at the two hospitals were invited to complete a 12-item survey. Descriptive statistics were calculated accordingly.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Almost 50% (132/256) responded; 98.4% owned a smartphone and 76% owned an iPhone. Seventy-nine percent used medical apps and 59% used the OLCHC formulary. Ninety-seven percent used smartphones for inter-team communication with 73.5% (n = 97) using WhatsApp. Smartphone camera was used by 57% for clinical photos and 41% for photos of radiological imaging. Only 42% reported obtaining consent for smartphone camera use from patients or guardians. Ninety-two percent either 'strongly agreed' or 'agreed' that smartphones positively impact their practice.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Smartphone usage is universal among healthcare professionals and their influence is growing in patient care.
